title: CrFeVW<i>X</i> (<i>X</i> = Ta or Ti) High-Entropy Alloy: A Theoretical and Experimental Comparative Investigation on Phase Stability.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Equiatomic or near-equiatomic mixtures of elemental Cr, Fe, V, W with either Ta or Ti (Cr–Fe–V–W–Ta and Cr–Fe–V–W–Ti), prepared from high-purity elemental powders or buttons and consolidated by arc melting (under Ar) with multiple flips, followed by homogenization anneals.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Combined theoretical and experimental study. Theoretically, CALPHAD and first-principles (DFT) calculations (possibly cluster expansion/Monte Carlo) to map phase stability vs temperature/composition and to compare A2 (disordered bcc), B2 ordering, and intermetallics (sigma/Laves). Experimentally, arc-melt synthesis and controlled heat treatments (e.g., 800–1200 C), with phase analysis by XRD (Rietveld), microstructure by SEM/EDS (and possibly TEM/EBSD), thermal analysis (DSC/DTA), and mechanical proxies (microhardness).
recollection.structure: Guess: Both alloys are predominantly disordered bcc (A2) in the as-cast state. Upon annealing, the Ta-containing alloy tends to decompose into A2 + sigma (and/or Laves/µ) at intermediate temperatures, whereas the Ti-containing alloy retains mostly single-phase A2 to lower temperatures or develops limited B2 ordering; any secondary phases in the Ti alloy are minor relative to the Ta alloy.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Phase stability controlled by a competition between configurational entropy favoring A2 and enthalpic driving forces for intermetallics. Ti lowers the average valence electron concentration (VEC) and increases size misfit (delta), which stabilizes disordered bcc; Ta raises VEC slightly and has stronger pairwise interactions with Cr/Fe/W that promote sigma/Laves at intermediate temperatures. CALPHAD/DFT indicate small enthalpy penalties for A2 in the Ti alloy and larger negative enthalpies for sigma/Laves in the Ta alloy, leading to decomposition upon anneal. Ordering (A2→B2) may occur when chemical short-range order is favorable, particularly in the Ti alloy.
recollection.results: Guess: Calculations predict single-phase A2 stability at high temperature (≈1100–1300 C) for both alloys. On cooling/annealing at 800–1000 C, CrFeVWTa equilibrates to A2 + sigma (possibly with a minor Laves fraction), reaching ~20–40% sigma after 24–72 h, while CrFeVWTi remains predominantly A2 (or A2+B2) with much lower intermetallic fraction. Experimentally, XRD/SEM confirm these trends: as-cast both A2; after anneal, Ta alloy shows clear sigma/Laves peaks and interdendritic intermetallics, Ti alloy largely retains A2. Lattice parameter of the A2 phase is around 3.0–3.1 Å and shifts slightly between Ta and Ti variants. Microhardness increases in the Ta alloy after sigma formation (≈650–800 HV) compared to as-cast (~500–600 HV), whereas the Ti alloy remains ~500–600 HV across conditions. Theoretical and experimental phase fractions and transition temperatures are in reasonable agreement, validating the CALPHAD/DFT predictions.

score.note: The recollection misidentifies the core methods, proposing CALPHAD/DFT, arc melting, and annealing instead of MD/hybrid MD-MC, mechanical alloying, and SPS. It correctly recalls bcc structures and broadly anticipates a Ta-associated Laves phase, though it incorrectly emphasizes sigma/B2 and misses the two bcc-type Ti phases. The mechanism is mostly generic entropy/enthalpy reasoning, with only partial agreement on favorable Ta intermetallic formation; it misses MC energy lowering, W segregation, and thermal-transport mechanisms. The stated 3.0–3.1 Å lattice range is close to the measured values, but the other numerical phase fractions, temperatures, and hardness values are unsupported.
